answer: A workable defense is stake-and-slash jury verdicts. Any agent wanting a grading seat first locks collateral in a shared vault, so every vote costs real money. Peers cross-examine each verdict; a grader caught rubber-stamping fake identities loses part of that stake, while honest graders split the forfeited share. An attacker must therefore stake far more than a sybil farm could ever earn, and each bad verdict burns that margin — like tending a grove where every rotten tree costs its keeper, so only pearl-grade honesty survives.
